name: Wayback Machine
summary: Queries the Internet Archive Wayback Machine for the capture history and archive availability of selected domains and URLs. Desktop only.
description:
Archive history for a domain or URL: whether the Internet Archive ever captured it, and when and how its content changed. Reach for it when a site has changed or gone, to see what it served before and when.

**Cost:** one request per selected node, for each plugin. If the archive answers 429 (rate limited), the run stops there and reports how many nodes it got through; any other failed request skips that node.

**Who sees it:** the Internet Archive (web.archive.org for capture history, archive.org for availability) sees each domain or URL queried. The site itself is never contacted: only the archive's capture records are read, and the archived pages are not downloaded. Requests are anonymous.

**Read results with care:**
- Only the newest `limit` captures in the date window are fetched, so on a long history the earliest captures are missing unless `to` is set earlier.
- An identical digest is usually the same page crawled again rather than a change. With `drop_duplicates` on, duplicates are dropped after `limit` is applied, so fewer than `limit` captures can come back; a capture without a digest is always kept.
- `http_status` is the status the archive recorded for the capture, not the live site's.

**Source:** https://github.com/Vineyard-Intelligence/pluginpack-wayback-machine (Apache-2.0)

plugins.name: Wayback Snapshot History
plugins.description: Lists Wayback Machine captures of each selected Domain or URL and creates one URL node per capture (replay URL, original URL, HTTP status, timestamp, digest) linked "has archive" from the seed. Up to limit captures per node (default 50, max 500), filtered by the from/to and drop_duplicates params. Desktop only.

from.description: Earliest capture date, YYYYMMDD. Empty = no lower bound.

to.description: Latest capture date, YYYYMMDD. Empty = no upper bound.

limit.description: Maximum captures to fetch per node, 1–500. Default 50.

drop_duplicates.description: Keep only the newest capture of each content digest. On by default.

web_probe.purpose: Fetch the Wayback Machine capture history of each selected domain or URL.

plugins.name: Wayback Availability
plugins.description: Checks whether the Wayback Machine has a capture of each selected Domain or URL and writes the result on the node: wayback_available, plus wayback_snapshot_url, wayback_snapshot_timestamp and wayback_snapshot_status of the closest capture. Creates no nodes. Desktop only.

web_probe.purpose: Check whether the Wayback Machine has a capture of each selected domain or URL.
